subject: [PATCH v5 5/7] mm/page_counter: introduce an asynchronous drainer

2026-08-31.patch_summary: This patch introduces an asynchronous drainer for page counters, which iterates through each CPU and flushes any existing charges without affecting unrelated memory cgroups' stock. This approach coalesces duplicate drain requests and improves performance by avoiding unnecessary work on remote CPUs.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt
reviews.summary: Questioned the need for an asynchronous drainer, suggesting that synchronous draining could be used instead. This led to a realization that the patch was trying to do two things at once and mixing up page_counter migration and scalable draining.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Aug 31, 2026 at 09:37:49AM -0700, Joshua Hahn wrote:
> The existing percpu memcg stock drainer schedules a stock drain worker
> per-cpu, one for every CPU containing the target memcg's stock.

But you are introducing remote draining. Why do you need async drainer at all?
Just always drain synchronously.

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn
reviews.summary: Acknowledged the concerns raised by Shakeel Butt and planned to post an updated version addressing them. This response indicates that the author is willing to revise the patch based on feedback.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, 7 Sep 2026 16:25:31 -0700 Shakeel Butt <shakeel.butt@linux.dev> wrote:

Hi Shakeel,

Thanks for your review on the series!

> On Mon, Aug 31, 2026 at 09:37:49AM -0700, Joshua Hahn wrote:
> > The existing percpu memcg stock drainer schedules a stock drain worker
> > per-cpu, one for every CPU containing the target memcg's stock.
> 
> But you are introducing remote draining. Why do you need async drainer at all?
> Just always drain synchronously.

I was trying to match parity with the existing code as much as possible.
But I see now that this series is a bit complicated because I'm trying
to do two things at once and mixing up the page_counter migration
and the scalable draining together.

In the next version I'll keep parity and only migrate to page_counter
and in a follow-up I'll address the drainers separately.

Thanks again!
Joshua

2026-09-07.patch_summary: This patch introduces an asynchronous drainer for the page_counter, which iterates through each CPU and flushes any existing charges, leaving unrelated memcgs' stock alone. This approach coalesces duplicate drain requests and allows for more efficient draining of page counters. The patch also updates the page_counter_drain_cpu_stock function to use a per-cpu raw_spinlock_t lock.
